title: GL.iNet Comet Q GL-RMQ1 Review A Single USB Type-C Cable Remote KVM Device with Tailscale
gist: ServeTheHome previews the GL.iNet Comet Q GL-RMQ1, a puck-shaped remote KVM that uses one USB Type-C cable for video, input and power, with WiFi for network. The excerpt covers the hardware overview and a boot-timing caveat.

insights.claim: The GL.iNet Comet Q GL-RMQ1 is a single-cable remote KVM: one USB Type-C cable carries power, video and keyboard, mouse and remote media to the target, with WiFi handling network, and it can also control phones and tablets.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Collapsing KVM cabling to one Type-C lead lowers the barrier to adding remote console access to small PCs and mobile devices.
insights.quote: Plug a USB Type-C cable into a device with a Type-C port that supports video, and that is the only cable you need.

insights.claim: The integrated, fixed Type-C cable is convenient but means there is no option for Type-A or Type-A plus HDMI connections.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: The design tradeoff limits compatibility with older or headless servers that lack video-capable Type-C.
insights.quote: It does, however, mean that if you wanted a Type-A connection, or a Type-A and HDMI, for example, the convenience is not there.

insights.claim: Because the unit is powered from the target, going from off to on can leave some systems booting faster than the KVM, making it hard to get into the BIOS.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: Power-through-the-target designs have a practical weakness for BIOS-level remote management.
insights.quote: If you go from off to on, some systems boot faster than the GL-RMQ1, so that makes it hard to get into the BIOS.

insights.claim: A 1.8-inch touchscreen shows the IP address and KVM and video status and handles WiFi setup, after which the unit is managed through a browser; a separate Type-C port provides power input for devices that have only one Type-C port.
insights.speaker: Eric Smith
insights.so_what: On-device setup and a pass-through power port address common single-port deployment issues.
insights.quote: Once the initial setup is done, you can then manage it via a browser.
